thread.title: Monthly-Pay Equity CEF Yields 7.7%, 11% Discount, Activist Investor Has Large Stake - Alpine Total Dynamic Dividend Fund (NYSE:AOD)

author: Rida Morwa
title: Monthly-Pay Equity CEF Yields 7.7%, 11% Discount, Activist Investor Has Large Stake - Alpine Total Dynamic Dividend Fund (NYSE:AOD)
text:
This report was jointly produced with author Julian Lin .
Thesis Aberdeen Total Dynamic Dividend ( AOD ), formerly named "Alpine Total Dynamic Dividend Fund," is a closed end fund (‘CEF’) with a primary investment objective of seeking high current dividend income, and a secondary investment objective of long-term growth of capital. It closed recently at $9.00 and its latest NAV is $10.09 per share. Trading at 10.8% discount to net asset value (‘NAV’), shares have received the attention of an activist fund which we believe will help drive management to close this NAV discount. It is currently paying a dividend of 5.75 cents per month for an annual dividend of 69 cents per share and a yield of 7.6%. This is an opportunity to buy shares of a high quality dividend CEF with a high 7.7% dividend yield while waiting for the closing of the NAV discount.
Some History: 2008 And The Bull Market Since Then AOD was launched in 2007 right before the financial crisis. AOD was hit hard during this tough period (as most other equities), and the current share price of $9 really does not come close to reaching the price shortly after initial issuance of around $40 per share. That said, this is a much different fund than before, with only 5.81% net current leverage compared to over 20% then .
Since the financial crisis, we have witnessed one of the longest bull rallies in history:
( Yahoo Finance )
After such a long bull run, some investors may question whether or not this can continue. Some may argue that the market cannot continue going up forever.
From the perspective of fundamental value investors, it is very relevant that this bull market is supported by growing corporate earnings. Since 2008, earnings for the S&P 500 Index have grown steadily:
(Chart by Author, data from multpl.com )
This means that when trying to figure out which stocks will outperform moving forward, we should be looking to see which stocks will continue to drive earnings growth. Certain conclusions can be reached by examining recent policy changes. For example, the lower corporate tax rate will benefit C corporations (almost all publicly traded stocks) generally. This will tend to push the entire market up as after-tax earnings (the key metric for stock valuation) increase throughout the market. In addition, the Federal Reserve is now forecasting several interest rate hikes this year. This should benefit certain financial stocks which depend upon interest rate "spreads" between the rates charged on loans and the rates paid on deposits. Money center and other banks like Bank of America ( BAC ) are poised to benefit. Another big factor is likely to be the lower tax rate on the repatriation of foreign earnings. This should benefit companies which have large amounts of cash and other assets held overseas as a result of foreign earnings. Such companies will benefit by being able to repatriate such funds and will also benefit on a go-forward basis with respect to their continuing stream of foreign earnings. Apple ( AAPL ) will be a huge beneficiary of this change because it holds an enormous amount of unrepatriated cash. As we will see below, AOD has positioned its portfolio to benefit from all of these trends.
We should remind investors that in spite of the strong history of the S&P 500, the U.S. stock market is not the only place to invest. In fact, many foreign markets are trading at lower price/earnings multiples at the very time when there is strong evidence of recovery in their economies. The European stock market has not enjoyed the same bullish run that the United States has been enjoying and sells for a reasonable 14.8 times earnings . Japan’s stock market has also been less exuberant than the United States market and it now sells for 16 times earnings . Exposure to other regions of the world may prove very profitable should they start to close their undervaluation to the USA stock market - that’s just a benefit of diversification.
All these reasons have led us to recommend AOD as it has positioned itself to benefit from these global mispricings and continue riding the U.S. bull market backed by earnings growth, all while paying a generous 7.7% dividend yield.
Getting To Know AOD AOD combines four research-driven investment strategies with the aim of identifying companies globally of all caps and sectors which have the potential for dividend growth and capital appreciation. The four strategies are:
Growth Value Special dividends Dividend capture rotation Dividend capture rotation involves rotating between stocks based on their ex-dividend dates in order to maximize quarterly dividend income. AOD pays a $0.0575 distribution monthly, and yields about 7.7% at recent prices. AOD has a 1.19% expense ratio which is in line with other equity CEFs.
The management of AOD has recently changed from Alpine to Aberdeen. Aberdeen is one of the best asset managers with a long and proven track record. Aberdeen noted that the current investment policies and strategies of the Funds will remain unchanged, so there will be continuity of strategy for the current strategy.
Fund Holdings AOD is most overweight the financials, industrials, information technology, and consumer discretionary sectors. All of these sectors are poised to benefit big from the current regulatory environment and strong economy:
As noted above, the sectors in which AOD is most heavily invested are the very sectors that are poised to benefit heavily from recent policy changes and economic trends. AOD is also diversified globally, although its heaviest exposure is to the United States stock markets.
The top ten holdings contain a nice mix of the strong dividend growth leaders of the modern age:
Share Price Performance AOD has outperformed the MSCI All Country Index over 1-, 3-, and 5-year periods. With a strong allocation to sectors benefiting from regulatory tailwind, we believe that this outperformance will continue moving forward:
NAV Discount AOD trades at substantial discount of nearly 11% to NAV. This represents a one year Z-Score of -1.50, which means AOD trades 1.5 standard deviations lower than its normal NAV discount. In the past 52 weeks, the range of the discount has been between a low of 7.17% and a high of 11.62%. Thus, the current discount is significantly above the mid-point of the range (which would be 9.4%). It is true that AOD has traded at even larger discounts in the past:
( CEFConnect )
However, we believe that activist involvement will be a catalyst to help narrow this discount in the near future (see section below).
Dividend History AOD has paid a steady $0.0575 monthly dividend for several years:
(CEFConnect)
Distributions historically have come from a combination of income and return of capital (‘ROC’):
(Chart by Author, data from CEFConnect)
We suspect many readers may see ROC and be alarmed. I must note that equity CEFs are different than “Fixed Income” CEFs as ROC for equity CEFs is not necessarily bad or “destructive.” In many cases, ROC could be a tax-efficient way to return capital to shareholders. If a CEF continues to achieve a high total return on its assets, then the distribution of capital to shareholders is not necessarily destructive of value.
Activist Likely to Help Close NAV Discount On January 18, Saba Capital Management, L.P., disclosed a 9.00% activist ownership in AOD . This represents a near 11% increase over its allocation in November of 2017. Saba Capital Management has a history of using activist management to help close NAV discounts at CEFs. In its “ Strategies ” page it discloses that “Saba selectively pursues an activist approach where corporate actions may be an effective tool to unlock shareholder value and monetize the discount to NAV.”
For a recent example of its activist efforts in action, one has to look no further than July of 2017, when Saba Capital Management successfully helped close the NAV gap at three Clough CEFs. Clough Global Dividend and Income Fund (NYSEMKT: GLV ), Global Equity Fund (NYSEMKT: GLQ ) and Global Opportunities Fund (NYSEMKT: GLO ) were all trading at NAV discounts of about 8% prior to the news. There the board of trustees agreed to a discount management program which included a tender offer for the fund shares and a managed distribution of 10%. We expect something similar to occur here at AOD with the NAV discount even more pronounced.
Bottom Line AOD has several advantages for the yield-oriented investor with reasonable confidence in the continued performance of global equity markets. It offers an attractive portfolio aimed at the sectors most likely to benefit from recent policy changes and economic trends. AOD has positioned itself to benefit both from the current regulatory environment and rising interest rates seen in USA markets, and also from the potential undervaluation of equities from other countries around the world.
AOD has a relatively large current discount to NAV when compared with other recent time periods. There are strong reasons to believe that this discount is likely to be reduced in the short to medium term future. With the activist firm Saba Capital Management taking a significant position and likely to work with management to close the NAV discount, AOD is attractively priced to potentially yield capital appreciation on top of its 7.7% dividend yield.
Investors get global exposure, solid management and a steady stream of dividends with a very attractive and highly likely "kicker" in the form of strong prospects that the discount to NAV will be reduced in coming months. AOD is a strong buy at the current price of $9.00 per share.
